title: A Red Blood Cell
subtitle: One complete circuit of the body
sourceNote: A complete circulation takes roughly a minute at rest. The timings of individual stages are illustrative — the anatomy is real, the second-by-second split is not precisely measurable.

waypoints.name: The aortic arch
waypoints.body: You have just been fired out of the left ventricle at about forty centimetres per second. This is the fastest you will move all trip.

waypoints.name: The descending aorta
waypoints.body: Heading down through the chest in a vessel about as wide as a garden hose, with the whole body still ahead of you.

waypoints.name: Into an arteriole
waypoints.body: The branching has begun. Each split makes the vessel narrower and the flow slower, which is exactly the point.

waypoints.name: A capillary
waypoints.body: You are now in a tube narrower than you are. Red blood cells fold into a bullet shape to squeeze through, single file.

waypoints.name: Oxygen unloaded
waypoints.body: The whole reason for the trip, and it takes under a second. Tissue takes the oxygen, you take away carbon dioxide.

waypoints.name: Into a venule
waypoints.body: The return journey begins. Veins are wider and lower pressure, so most of your minute is spent on this half.

waypoints.name: The vena cava
waypoints.body: The body's largest vein, carrying you back towards the heart. Valves and the squeeze of your muscles do much of the work.

waypoints.name: The right side of the heart
waypoints.body: Through the right atrium and into the right ventricle. Note that you have not been to the lungs yet — that comes next.

waypoints.name: The pulmonary artery
waypoints.body: The only artery in the body carrying oxygen-poor blood, heading for the lungs.

waypoints.name: The alveoli
waypoints.body: Oxygen reloaded in about three quarters of a second, across a membrane less than a thousandth of a millimetre thick.

waypoints.name: The pulmonary vein
waypoints.body: Back towards the heart, bright red again, in the only vein that carries oxygen-rich blood.

waypoints.name: The left ventricle again
waypoints.body: One full circuit. You will do this about fourteen hundred times a day, for a hundred and twenty days, covering roughly five hundred kilometres before you are recycled.
